asr.full_text: I'm over at blockchain.info and if we just go to the top of the page here and click on charts and then we're gonna scroll down to where it says mining information and we're gonna click on a hash rate distribution here and just select last 24 hours and zoom in and you will see that in the last 24 hours that Bitclub Network has 2% of the market and is in the top 10 mining pools in the world and if we click on the last 4 days you can see that Bitclub Network has 3.5% So if we scroll down the page further now and look for bitclub, there we have bitclub network. I'm going to click on that which brings us to this page here at blockchain.info where it shows the recent blocks done by Club network, and it gives you the block heights here and the dates and time here and the hash here. So you can see that on the 27th, we are just starting the 27th, so there's one block shown here, and on the 26th, you can see there's 1, 2, 3, 4 blocks there and the 25th 1, three four five six seven eight nine and so on so on all the way down so if we just click on any of these hashes here click on the top one and now you can see here is the block number and this tells you the total estimated transaction volume and transaction fees and the block reward, , which is worth 28,500 US dollars, so you can see that Bitclub network is a genuine mining pool and they are collecting huge amounts of Bitcoin from mining and you can verify here it's 12.5 bitcoins plus the transaction fee of 4.37 and you you see the total here 16.8 BItcoins, with the value of $38,500 almost. And you can see here that these are newly generated coins, so these are newly mined coins which is why there is's no transaction number underneath there. This shows you that BitClub Network is a real mining company and GENERALLY mined in bitcoin. And inside the BitClub website you can actually click on pool stats and get real-time statistics about their stats and the pool hash rate and again if you scroll down here these are the different names of the servers or machines which are mining bitcoins for a bit club pools and again you can click on any of these hash height block height numbers here and get to the hash again back on blockchain.info and click on the hash again and get the same information which I just showed you so this proves that they are mining Bitcoins they are one of the top 10 mining pools in the world and anybody who tells you that Bitclub is not real or is not mining then this is how you can prove that they are just just go over to blockchain.info, go to the charts and Scroll down to the mining pools Hashrate distribution and it will show you the mining pools here and it only shows the top mining pools in the world and Bitcoin is in the top 10 the big club networks are is in the top ten yeah so that should dispel any myth or that people say that Bitcoin is not a real mining pool or they say some crazy stuff like Bitcoin is also Ponzi you can also come inside the Bitcoin website again here and it says can bit club met Network verify the mining and as they say yeah we have a public mining pool where you can track passion pair were it real time the website address which is what just showed you and you can view the big coin pool on the blockchain here and detail records here which is what I just showed you. So no Bitcoin Club Network is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi scheme has no product it's just a money game set up to pay people with other people's money and eventually they will crash and burn. So what bitcoin mining is, is it's mining brand new bitcoins verifying transactions for the bitcoin network for which they get paid a mining fee. They mine new bitcoins. These bitcoins are shared out between the pool share members and paid on daily so when you purchase a share in BitClub you're actually purchasing a share in mining equipment and you earn profits from what's being mined every day and this is a good thing about Bitcoin as I've mentioned that you can't trick it, you can't fake it everything is recorded in a public ledger for everyone to see so while bitcoin is secure and private it allows you to send transactions almost anonymously so there is no paper trail, it is still a public ledger of hashed, hashes and transactions that can be verified and viewed anytime in order to verify that a transaction has actually taken place. Subscribe!

textual.observation: The speaker promotes purchasing a BitClub share as a share in mining equipment and claims members earn profits from mined Bitcoin on a daily basis.

evidence.quote: when you purchase a share in BitClub you're actually purchasing a share in mining equipment
you earn profits from what's being mined every day
These bitcoins are shared out between the pool share members and paid on daily

textual.context: Promotional explanation; the speaker presents the arrangement as legitimate and rejects the Ponzi characterization.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised recurring financial return is directly linked to purchasing a share and participating in member payouts.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether payments occurred, the applicable fees or conditions, or whether the stated mining activity supports the claimed returns.

textual.observation: The speaker directs viewers to blockchain.info and BitClub website statistics to support the claim that BitClub is a genuine, top-10 Bitcoin mining pool.

evidence.quote: I'm over at blockchain.info and if we just go to the top of the page here and click on charts
so you can see that Bitclub network is a genuine mining pool
it will show you the mining pools here and it only shows the top mining pools in the world

textual.context: Promotional and defensive context; the speaker uses the referenced sites as purported support against claims that BitClub is not real or is a Ponzi.
textual.potential_relevance: A claimed organizational identity and mining status are tied to an instruction to inspect external site data.
textual.limitations: The records do not independently verify the sites, displayed statistics, BitClub's identity, or the accuracy of the conclusions drawn from them.

visual.observation: A webpage promotes BitClub Network as “THE MOST INNOVATIVE AND LUCRATIVE WAY TO EARN BITCOIN” and tells viewers to “JOIN BITCLUB NETWORK”; a later frame displays the destination text “Bitcoin.roseandmorris.com.”
visual.context: Promotional webpage presentation with sign-up and member-login options visible.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised lucrative Bitcoin return is directly linked to joining a named network and visiting a displayed destination.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether the promised returns occurred, whether the destination was reached, or whether the promotion was legitimate.

visual.observation: An illustrated BitClub Network presentation shows a money bag and the partially visible text “$10,000 for one bitcoin in...” beside BitClub branding.
visual.context: Animated or illustrated promotional presentation; the full claim is not visible.
visual.potential_relevance: A large monetary claim is visually associated with BitClub Network branding, which may merit review as a stated return claim.
visual.limitations: The text is partially obscured, so the timeframe or full conditions cannot be determined; no payment or transaction outcome is shown.

visual.observation: A chat exchange states, “But Dan, bitclub is also a ponzi,” followed by a response, “lol it a mining pool my friend,” and “no ponzi.... genuine bitcoin mining.”
visual.context: Visible discussion and conflicting characterization of BitClub; the exchange includes both an allegation and an explicit denial.
visual.potential_relevance: The source explicitly reports a disputed claim about the structure of the Bitcoin-earning opportunity, while preserving the contrary explanation.
visual.limitations: The exchange does not establish which characterization is accurate or provide independent evidence about the organization’s operation.

textual_context_notes.observation: The title frames the material as a review or question about whether Bitclub Network is a scam or Ponzi scheme.

evidence.quote: Is Bitclub Network a Scam or Ponzi scheme?

textual_context_notes.observation: The description references revshares and Ponzi schemes allegedly shutting down or running away with people's money.

evidence.quote: If you are tired of revshares shutting down or ponzi schemes and hiyp's running away with people's money

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker explicitly denies that BitClub Network is a Ponzi scheme and describes a Ponzi scheme as paying people with other people's money.

evidence.quote: So no Bitcoin Club Network is not a Ponzi scheme.
A Ponzi scheme has no product it's just a money game set up to pay people with other people's money

visual_context_notes.observation: A visible mining-pool page presents pool statistics including round duration, block difficulty, shares, and effective hash rate.
A blockchain block page displays transaction counts, Bitcoin totals, fees, and a relay attribution to BitClub Network.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes BitClub as a lucrative way to earn Bitcoin, tells viewers to join, provides a related destination address, and links participation to purchasing a mining share that allegedly pays mined bitcoin and profits daily. Although it shows blockchain and pool-statistics pages and denies that BitClub is a Ponzi, those materials are presented to support the join-and-earn offer rather than merely report on it. The video's disputed-status chat and incomplete "$10,000 for one bitcoin in..." text do not establish an additional specific promised return.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The speaker describes buying a share in mining equipment and links that purchase to daily profits from mining and daily distributions to pool-share members.

evidence.observation: The title frames the video as a review questioning BitClub Network.
evidence.quote: Is Bitclub Network a Scam or Ponzi scheme? See full Bitclub Network review here.

evidence.quote: when you purchase a share in BitClub you're actually purchasing a share in mining equipment and you earn profits from what's being mined every day

evidence.observation: The speaker claims mined bitcoins are distributed to pool-share members daily.
evidence.quote: These bitcoins are shared out between the pool share members and paid on daily

evidence.observation: A BitClub Network page describes joining as a lucrative way to earn Bitcoin and displays a join prompt.
The join-and-earn page is shown with the displayed address Bitcoin.roseandmorris.com.
The speaker explicitly denies the Ponzi characterization.
evidence.quote: So no Bitcoin Club Network is not a Ponzi scheme.

evidence.observation: A block-summary page displays transaction information and lists BitClub Network in its Relayed By field.
A displayed chat includes an allegation that BitClub is a Ponzi and replies describing it as genuine Bitcoin mining.
